correctness.rationale: Reduction theorem verified by hand: for G on 35 vertices plus new vertex v with neighbourhood S, a K4 using v exists iff S contains a triangle of G, and an independent 6-set using v exists iff some independent 5-set of G lies in V\S, so extension is exactly a triangle-free set meeting all independent 5-sets. Machine proof independently rerun: frozen verifier reproduced all 37 graphs valid (K4=0, no independent 6-set) and all 37 PROVED-NO-EXTENSION in 12s with per-graph independent-5 counts 742-818 and node counts 2491-5800 matching noext_proof_summary.json exactly. Spot brute-force cross-check with itertools.combinations on graphs 0/14/26 confirmed K4=0, indep6=0 and indep5=784/742/797 matching the verifier. Branch-and-bound (fail-first branching on uncovered family, triangle-closure pruning) is exhaustive; two independent implementations agreed per the report. Scope honestly limited to the 37-graph ledger, not all extremal graphs.

originality.rationale: EMERGENT_FINDING route verified as genuine: single-vertex extension of the provided 35-vertex corpus is the necessary first step of the R(4,6)>=37 target, pursued before de-novo search, and submitted only after the target blocked. Live fused retrieval (SerpBase/OpenAlex/Crossref, all providers ok, no partial failure) plus full fetch of the decisive primary source shows the 37 witnesses themselves are prior (Exoo 2012 improved R(4,6) from 35 to 36 with 37 new K35 colorings) but the maximality theorem is new: Exoo proves existence/lower bound only, Radziszowski Small Ramsey Numbers survey and MathWorld/House of Graphs tables record only bounds (R(4,6) in 36..41) and witness existence, and no census, classification, database entry, dual/complement encoding, or stronger theorem implies or exhaustively covers per-graph triangle-free-hitting-set nonexistence. Report claims no originality for witnesses or reduction, only for the systematic maximality computation with exact certificates and frozen verifier.

value.rationale: The headline is a rigorously established exact invariant of a specific natural object class motivated before computation: the entire known corpus establishing the current best lower bound R(4,6)>=36, and the invariant (single-vertex-extension maximality) is exactly the cheapest route to R(4,6)>=37. The value was not known or mechanically implied, a future Ramsey searcher can reasonably need the precise fact plus the 12-second reusable verifier/ledger, and the result converts a blocked existence target into a durable obstruction theorem (any 36-witness must be de-novo and avoid all 37 graphs). Honest limitation to the ledger rather than all extremal graphs does not erase the headline under the shared standard. This is not a textbook restatement, parameter substitution, tiny unmotivated gain, or unexplained enumeration: exact per-graph certificates (742-818 families, 2491-5800 nodes), obstruction diagnostics, and reuse artifacts are given.

Fused scope_literature_search over literal, equivalent/dual, and dominance directions (SerpBase Top 10 + OpenAlex Top 15 + Crossref Top 15 per query, 20 fused results, all 9 provider/query slots ok, partial=false): nearest hits are Exoo R(4,6) paper, Chung-Grinstead/Fan survey, Goedgebeur-Radziszowski R(3,k) bounds, and generic Ramsey references; none states or implies no-extension of the 37-graph corpus.

broader_coverage.evidence: Known general results are asymptotic (e.g. Mattheus-Verstraete R(4,t) Omega(t^3/log^4 t)), recursive upper bounds, and the open interval 36<=R(4,6)<=41 per Radziszowski/MathWorld. No completed census or classification of Ramsey(4,6;36) graphs exists; R(4,6) remains open, and upper-bound techniques (e.g. e(3,k,n) enumeration for R(3,k)) do not decide extensions of these specific 35-vertex (4,6)-graphs.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A broader theorem would cover the claim only if it classified all 36-vertex (4,6)-graphs or proved nonexistence (R=36). Since the interval is still open and no such census exists, the maximality claim is not a special case or corollary of a stronger known fact.
broader_coverage.search: Searched for stronger/broader coverage: R(4,6) upper bounds and exact value, exhaustive census or classification of Ramsey(4,6;36) graphs, larger-parameter Ramsey classification covering n=36 as a special case.

claim_vs_prior_implication.evidence: Exoo 2012 abstract and metadata prove exactly: 37 colorings of K35 with no K4 in color 1 and no K6 in color 2, hence R(4,6)>=36. The paper presents one symmetric coloring in detail from heuristic search. It contains no triangle-free-hitting-set analysis, no per-graph independent-5-set counts (742-818), no proof-node certificates (2491-5800), and no statement that none of the 37 graphs embeds in a 36-vertex witness.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Existence of 37 witnesses does not imply none of them extends by one vertex; extension is a further universal-existential property requiring exhaustive search over all 2^35 neighbourhoods per graph modulo triangle constraints. The submitted proof adds that property, so the headline is not implied by, and not a recomputation/certificate/repackaging of, Exoo.
claim_vs_prior_implication.search: Compared submitted maximality headline literally against Exoo 2012 hypotheses and conclusions: existence of 37 Ramsey(4,6;35) witnesses versus proved nonexistence of single-vertex extensions for each of the 37 ledger graphs.

equivalent_formulations.evidence: Fused search over dual/complement/matrix encodings returned only generic Ramsey-theory references (Ramsey theorem pages, R(5,5)/R(6,6) discussion, graph-class Ramsey numbers) and the Exoo paper; no source states the same obstruction as complement K6-free graphs with clique number at most 5 and independence number at most 3, incidence/adjacency-matrix hitting sets, or triangle-free neighbourhood language.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The complement dual (K6-free H on 35 vertices with omega<=5) and algebraic/incidence encodings describe the same objects but no prior source proves the corresponding dual maximality (no one-vertex co-extension). Synonymous notation therefore does not supply prior coverage.
equivalent_formulations.search: Searched equivalent formulations: complement (6,4)/(4,6) dual graphs with omega<=5 and alpha<=3, K6-free formulation, triangle-free hitting-set / transversal and incidence-graph / adjacency-matrix encodings of one-vertex Ramsey extension.

exact_database_or_table.evidence: Radziszowski Small Ramsey Numbers survey table, MathWorld Ramsey Number table, and House of Graphs Ramsey-numbers meta-directory record bounds and known witness existence (R(4,6) lower bound 36 from Exoo 37 graphs) but list no per-graph extension-maximality field, no independent-5-set counts, and no no-extension certificates. Ledger r46data.g6 graph6 strings are the lane working copy of the known corpus, not a new database entry claiming the witnesses themselves as novel.
exact_database_or_table.reasoning: A table/database covers the claim only if the exact parameter (per-graph single-vertex non-extendability of each of the 37 graphs) already appears there. Since tables record only the bound and existence, the maximality invariant is not a direct lookup or known-database recomputation.
exact_database_or_table.search: Searched exact-parameter coverage in official tables and databases: Radziszowski Small Ramsey Numbers R(4,6) entry, House of Graphs Ramsey directory, McKay-type graph data, and graph6 ledger tables for 35-vertex Ramsey(4,6) witnesses with maximality flags.

material_sources.relationship_to_claim: Lehavia arXiv:2411.04267v1 Section 5.1 proves only that no 36-vertex graph has at least max(4,6)+1=7 distinct 35-vertex subgraphs among the 37 known Ramsey(4,6;35) counterexamples (20-second check), under a method whose Algorithm 2 generates only graphs with at least 2 known subgraphs; it does not decide the >=1-subgraph question, i.e. per-graph single-vertex extension, so its hypothesis is strictly stronger and its conclusion strictly weaker than the submitted maximality theorem.

perplexity_final_check.rationale: Terminal Perplexity search added useful incremental recall beyond the base providers: McKay Ramsey Graphs database page (r46_35some.g6 ledger, open 36-40 vertex possibility) and Lehavia arXiv:2411.04267v1 one-vertex-extension algorithm with an R(4,6,36) check. Both were verified in full (Lehavia HTML Sections 1-6 fetched) and literally compared: McKay records only witness existence, and Lehavia proves only the >=7-known-subgraphs emptiness (a consequence of, not a substitute for, the submitted >=1-subgraph per-graph no-extension theorem) while explicitly noting Exoo did not prove non-generability and its own Algorithm 2 covers only graphs with at least 2 known subgraphs. Remaining hits duplicate base coverage (Exoo paper, Small Ramsey Numbers survey, House of Graphs, R(3,k) bounds) or are keyword-similar only (K6-free class page, unrelated Ramsey variants). No returned source states, implies, or exhaustively covers per-graph triangle-free-hitting-set nonexistence, so originality PASS is preserved and no verdict change occurs.

residual_risks: Quantifier is over the 37-graph provided ledger, which may not exhaust all Ramsey(4,6;35) graphs; a de-novo 36-witness or an extension of an unlisted 35-witness remains possible, as honestly stated.

Machine-checked proof trusts the correctness of the frozen Python verifier, graph6 parser, and stdlib execution environment; mitigated by two independent implementations, exact node-count agreement, brute-force spot checks, and a 12-second rerunnable artifact.
Bounded stochastic de-novo search batteries are non-convergence evidence only, not a nonexistence proof; they are reported as context, not part of the headline maximality theorem.
